text.p: These are the leading stories in Bosnian press on Tuesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President of Bosnia's Serb entity, Biljana Plavsic, says she was probably victim of attempted putsch orchestrated by former president Radovan Karadzic, who she accused of blocking state instiutions.

- Slovenia informed 2,000 Bosnian refugees that their refugee status will end by July 31. This measure applies to refugees who can safely return to the entity where they lived before the war, while those whose return might put them in danger will be allowed to stay longer.

- Bosnian ambassador to Croatia Kasim Trnka says Croatia insists on Izetbegovic-Tudjman meeting only to try to demonstrate to international community its support for peace. By putting blame on the Moslem side, Croats try to hide their own lack of cooperation, Trnka says.
- Party of Democratic Action (SDA) in Capljina requests that the registration process in the town be annulled because of alleged irregularities which allowed 4,500 Croats to register.

- Robert Gelbard, special U.S. envoy to Bosnia, seriously warned Croat and Moslem leaders in Mostar about possible consequences for both sides unless all agreements reached so far are implemented. Gelbard said Washington will stick by its support for Moslem-Croat federation, says deputy mayor of Mostar, Safet Orucevic.

- OSCE spokesman David Foley said at least 2.4 million voters have registered for the forthcoming local elections. The voter registration process is completed except for the town of Brcko where registration has been extended until July 12.
- Independent media in Banja Luka in the Serb entity said they lost electric power after reporting on Plavsic's order to suspend Interior Minister Dragan Kijac. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
